messages:
alex: Quick heads up — brought rk7b int4 into shadowbench today. NDCG@5 looks fine (+0.2%) but MRR@10 is down ~6% vs baseline. Drop is concentrated on short queries and docs returned by the sparse retriever. Anyone seen this interaction before? :thinking:

maria: Can you paste the exact eval config/flags used? sometimes tokenization or preprocess mismatch causes spuriously bad MRR.

kevin: Also did we change candidate normalization? we used to strip leading punctuation for sparse docs in the old pipeline. small formatting diffs can flip ranks.

alex: Config snippet I used: `model=rk7b-int4 clamp=true batch=16 kv_cache=false tokenizer=v2 norm=on seed=42 preproc=eval-default`
Quick numbers from shadowbench run: `MRR@10 baseline=0.422 -> new=0.397 (-5.93%, p<0.01)`

sophie: First isolate retrieval vs reranker: run dense-only candidates and sparse-only. If dense-only is fine, then it's the candidate mix or formatting. Also try turning priming off.

alex: Dense-only run already done: delta ~ -0.5% (essentially noise). So the issue shows up when sparse candidates are present (sparse-only run: -5.6%). That points to either formatting of sparse docs or a candidate-length/priming interaction.

kevin: Do we have examples of sparse docs that contain HTML or leading markdown bullets? those can change tokenization length and attention distribution.

maria: Another frequent mismatch: prod retrieval pipeline lowercases and strips HTML, but eval harness may not. Can you check pipeline parity?

alex: Repro command I'm using: `./run_eval --snapshot rk7b-int4 --candidates retriever=sparse --preproc=prod --seed=42 --metrics=mrr,ndcg --sample=10k`
I'll try both `--preproc=prod` and `--preproc=eval-default` and compare token sequences.

ci-bot: Shadowbench job #8792 finished. Summary: ndcg@5 +0.1%, mrr@10 -5.8% on sample=10k. Artifacts: s3://redwood-shadow/rk7b-int4/8792/ (logs and per-query diffs).

sophie: Next ablation suggestions: 1) sparse-only with html-strip and collapse-whitespace, 2) sparse-only with tokenizer=v1, 3) sparse-only with priming disabled. Keep batch/seed fixed.

alex: Scheduling ablation runs now: 1) sparse-only untouched, 2) sparse-only html-strip, 3) sparse-only html-strip + lowercase, 4) tokenizer v1. Will post per-run MRR/ndcg and a tiny sample of failure queries.

maria: If this proves to be a harness mismatch, we should add an onboarding gate: preproc parity check between prod retrieval and eval harness. If token sequence diff rate > 1% for top-k tokens, block rollout.

alex: Agreed — I'll add a small script to assert normalized token sequences equal across both pipelines and include it in the onboarding checklist + the model bring-up README.

sophie: Nice. Also leave a short note in the bring-up doc with the exact repro command and a link to the shadow artifacts. Helps future triage.

alex: Will do. Posting interim results here when ablations finish. Thanks all :thumbsup:
